long_description:
Overview

Chill with NESST Skool online, turn brain freeze into exam ease—let’s nail it together! For parents and neurodiverse students Yrs 9-13

Brain Freeze to Exam Ease Free Information Session




Join us online for an introduction to NESSTSkool – Brain Freeze to Nailed It!, an online learning community supporting neurodiverse students in Years 9–13 as they prepare for tests, assessments and exams.

When a student’s mind goes blank in an exam, knowing the subject isn’t always enough. Sometimes they need practical strategies to regulate, retrieve what they know and express it effectively.

In this information session, you’ll discover how Brain Freeze to Nailed It! complements the work of schools and tutors by focusing on the strategies around learning and exams — rather than teaching subject content.

We’ll introduce the six learning zones:

❤️ Regulation Zone → 🧠 Memory Lab → 📚 Subject Vault → ✍ Expression Studio → 🎯 Exam Ready → 🌱 Progress Wins

You’ll also get a look inside the Skool community, find out about the resources, coaching, Brain Thaw Student Café and Parent Café, and learn how the freemium model works.

There’ll be time for questions too, so come along and see whether Brain Freeze to Nailed It! could help your student move from Brain Freeze to Exam Ease.

When the mind goes blank, strategy matters.

long_description:
Overview

Clear winter’s heaviness and awaken your natural aliveness through a gentle somatic breathwork journey into greater clarity and presence.

Somatic Breathwork: Spring Cleanse & Rise




Starts at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

Spring is a threshold, the season the body naturally wants to clear out, lighten, and open.

Spring Cleanse & Rise is a 60-minute somatic breathwork journey that works on two levels at once. First, we clear: releasing the heaviness, fog, and holding that can settle in over winter. Then, from that cleaner, quieter space, we open, using the breath as a doorway into a deeper, more spacious state of awareness.

Because when the body has less to carry, something else can move. A subtle, rising sense of aliveness. A feeling of connection to something larger and quieter within you. Many people describe it as coming home to a part of themselves they'd forgotten was there.

This is that experience made accessible, no belief system required, no experience needed. Just your breath, a safe and consent-led container, and a willingness to meet what opens.

Through a trauma-aware breathwork arc, we'll support your system to:

release the stagnation, weight, and fatigue carried through winter
soften the guarding that keeps you stuck in your head
let a natural, rising energy move up and through the body
open, gently, into a more expansive and connected state of awareness

You'll leave feeling lighter, clearer, and quietly awake, grounded in your body and open to more.

Who this is for

This session is for you if:

you can feel spring's shift but you're still carrying winter in your body
you've felt heavy, foggy, flat, or stuck in your head
your chest or breath has felt tight, shallow, or braced
you're curious about deeper, more expansive states, but put off by dogma or jargon
you want something that genuinely lands in the body, not just another idea to think about
you're new to breathwork and want a welcoming, choice-based space to begin

What to expect

Arrival (consent + information), chair, side-lying, and low-intensity options available
Guided breath arrival and brief body scan to ground and centre
Breath demonstration + choice of intensity tracks (including a gentle nasal-only option)
A guided somatic breathwork arc, clearing first, then opening, steady and body-led
Optional movement to support release (micro-shakes, shaking, or gentle unwinding)
Space to rest in whatever opens, spacious, quiet, supported
Integration rest + grounding
Closing reflection (brief journaling prompt or quiet pause)

Benefits you may notice

You might experience:

a lighter body and a clearer, more spacious mind
more warmth, aliveness, and energy moving through you
a felt sense of connection, presence, and inner spaciousness
emotional release without overwhelm
deeper, easier breathing
a steadier, more awake baseline that stays with you

What to bring

Please bring:

Warm layers (we'll warm up, but your body may cool during rest)
Water bottle
Small towel
Optional eye mask or light scarf
Journal and pen

Pre-class prep

Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior.
Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
If you have health conditions, please check with your provider.
Feel free to email Lynn at hi@lynofuro.co.nz if there's anything you'd like to share before the session.

Contraindications and safety

Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy, serious cardiovascular conditions, uncontrolled blood pressure, glaucoma or retinal detachment, epilepsy or seizure history, recent surgery or concussion, or severe psychiatric conditions/active psychosis. A conservative, nasal-only track is always available. This is not a substitute for medical care.

Aftercare

After the session, remember to:

Drink plenty of water
Eat nourishing food
Engage in simple movement or a short walk
Journal your insights
Get an early bedtime

Emotional waves may continue for 24 to 48 hours. Reach out if you need support.


You'll also receive a guided audio breathwork aftercare to support you in the 24 to 48 hours after the session, with gentle regulation, grounding, and integration.

Event followed by a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert! All included in your ticket.
About Lynn (Facilitator)

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Lynn supports people who are high-functioning on the outside but chronically tense, exhausted, or quietly stuck on the inside.

Lynn's work blends three pillars:

Somatic breathwork to regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline in the body
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, and deep rest, in a gentle, consent-based way
Life coaching to translate what opens in session into real change in relationships, work, boundaries, and daily life

Lynn's approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn't on forcing anything, it's on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, open, and remember its natural capacity for calm and connection.

1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching, a spot is open

If you felt a yes in your body during this session, you're invited to go deeper. Lynn is opening a private 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching spot for someone ready to work with nervous system regulation, somatic inquiry, breathwork, and grounded life coaching support.

To enquire, DM "rise" on Instagram or email hi@lynofuro.co.nz with the subject line: October 1:1.




Booking and policies
Doors close 5 minutes after the start.
Refunds or transfers are as per Bhakti Lounge policy.


Questions before you join? Email hi@lynofuro.co.nz and Lynn will support you.

long_description:
Overview

Join Massey Chancellor and former-Toyota CEO Alistair Davis for a drink and some inspiring business and leadership lessons.

This month:
ALISTAIR DAVIS is Chancellor of Massey University and former CEO and Chair of Toyota New Zealand. He is a distinguished leader whose career spans over four decades in motoring, business, sustainability, and service.

Come and listen to his hot tips on leadership, on building your business one step at a time, and how to leverage your team's advantage in tough times.

Alistair Davis was Toyota CEO from 2008 until his retirement in mid‑2020, during which time he led Toyota to a record 32 consecutive years as New Zealand’s top-selling car brand.

A vocal advocate for climate action, Davis co-founded the Climate Leaders Coalition in 2018 alongside major businesses, backing the Zero Carbon Act. Honoured as an Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit in 2021, his recognition reflects service spanning motoring, business, and sustainability.

Davis retains governance roles with Toyota NZ, Toyota Australia, and Toyota Finance, and was appointed Chancellor of Massey University in March 2024. In his role, he balances diverse stakeholder interests – from students and academics to taxpayers and the environment – and advocates for financial resilience, academic excellence, Te Tiriti partnership, and sustainability.

name: Quarterly Planning Session: Escape The Owner Trap

Paraparaumu Beach Golf Club
Paraparaumu Beach, Wellington Region
long_description:
Overview

Step away from the day-to-day, remove the bottlenecks keeping everything dependent on you, and build a focused 90-day plan.

Give yourself one clear day to plan the next 90 days

Most business owners do not struggle because they lack ideas.

They struggle because the day-to-day keeps taking over.

Customers need answers. Staff have questions. Quotes need to go out. Jobs run late. The important planning work gets pushed to next week, next month or the next quarter.

The Escape Plan is a practical quarterly planning session for business owners who need space to think clearly, make decisions and set a focused direction for the next 90 days.

It is not a day of vague goal-setting.

It is not about creating a complicated plan that ends up sitting in a drawer.

It is a working session where you will review what has happened, decide what matters now and turn your priorities into practical actions.

During the session, you will:
Review the past quarter honestly
Recognise what worked and what did not
Identify the issues consuming your time and attention
Clarify what the business needs from the next 90 days
Select a small number of meaningful priorities
Decide what should be stopped, simplified or delegated
Turn your priorities into clear actions
Build a practical quarterly plan to take back to your team
Create accountability around the commitments you make
Who should attend?

The Escape Plan is designed for business owners who:

Feel caught in the daily demands of the business
Have too many competing priorities
Keep carrying unfinished projects into the next quarter
Know changes are needed but have not made time to plan them properly
Want clearer direction for themselves and their team
Are ready to make practical decisions about what happens next

You do not need a polished strategy document.

You do not need to have all your numbers perfectly organised.

Bring the real business.

Bring the unfinished issues, the decisions you have been avoiding and the priorities that keep getting pushed aside.

What will you leave with?

By the end of the day, you will have:

A clearer view of where your business stands

Join us for the next Café des Idées - Multilingual kids & Multi-skilled teachers, multilingual education in France and Aotearoa New Zealand

The next Café des Idées, organised by FAST! – France Aotearoa Science, Technology & !nnovation and Alliance Française Wellington, is honoured to host Dr Fiona Smythe and Dr Rosemary Erlam for a captivating discussion on multilingual kids and the multi-skilled teachers who support them in France and Aotearoa New Zealand.

With growing numbers of multilingual children in schools on both sides of the world, teachers face real challenges supporting heritage languages alongside French or English. Drawing on research from France and Aotearoa, and a new bilateral project between Université de Bordeaux and the University of Auckland, our speakers share what it takes to turn linguistic diversity into a classroom strength.

Dr Fiona Smythe is a Postdoctoral Researcher at l'Université de Bordeaux and a FAST! Vincent Salomon Travel Award recipient. Dr Rosemary Erlam is Associate Professor at the University of Auckland, leading its Postgraduate Certificate/Diploma in Teaching Linguistically Diverse Learners.

long_description:
Overview

A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, deep connection and brotherhood in a space of trust, presence and belonging.

Men's Circle: Brotherhood & Belonging




Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

The evening creates a supportive space for men to come together, connect, and speak openly about life. Whether you’re moving through change, seeking deeper connection, or simply looking for a place where you can show up as you are, you’re welcome here.

The conversations are honest, real, and grounded in respect. There’s no pressure to speak, share, or have all the answers. Listening is just as welcome. Together, we create a space rooted in confidentiality and non-judgement, where everyone can feel safe, heard, and genuinely themselves.

Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.
After the circle, stay for a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert ($20 or $10 for students). Sharing a meal is a simple way to extend the sense of community and connection. This gathering is offered on a non-profit basis.
Meet Your Host: Sri Jiva

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

I'm so excited to be bringing this workshop for the third time to Nelson this Sept 2026.

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)


Sunday 20th Sept - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2:00 - 4:00pm


Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

10:30am - 12:30pm or 2-4pm
